title: Finding Kissing Numbers with Game-theoretic Reinforcement Learning
abstract: arXiv:2511.13391v5 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Since Isaac Newton first studied the Kissing Number Problem in 1694, determining the maximal number of non-overlapping spheres around a central sphere has remained a defining challenge in discrete geometry. As the local analogue of Hilbert's 18th problem, it has profound implications across geometry, number theory and information theory. Although lattices and codes have achieved significant progress, the field is confined to isolated extremal configurations, leaving underlying geometric principles obscured. Here we shift the object to the broader extremal configuration space, thereby opening a new path for the Kissing Number Problem. Accordingly, we recast this problem as a cooperative matrix-completion game, and train a reinforcement learning system, PackingStar, to solve it. translated_title: 利用博弈论强化学习寻找吻接数
translated_abstract: 自1694年艾萨克·牛顿首次研究吻接数问题以来，确定围绕一个中心球体可放置的互不重叠球体的最大数量，一直是离散几何中一个标志性的难题。作为希尔伯特第18问题的局部类比，它在几何学、数论和信息论中都具有深远的影响。尽管格与码的研究已取得重大进展，但该领域仍局限于孤立的极值构型，使潜在的几何原理变得模糊不清。在本研究中，我们将研究对象转移到更广泛的极值构型空间，从而为吻接数问题开辟了一条新路径。据此，我们将该问题重新表述为一个协作式矩阵补全博弈，并训练了一个名为 PackingStar 的强化学习系统来求解它。其中一个玩家负责填充余弦条目，另一个玩家负责纠正次优条目，从而使爆炸性增长的几何复杂性变得可以处理。（注：原摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文将经典的吻接数问题重新表述为协作式矩阵补全博弈，并训练强化学习系统 PackingStar，通过两个玩家分别填充与纠正余弦条目来探索更广泛的极值构型空间，为这一离散几何难题开辟了新的求解路径。
en_tdlr: The paper recasts the classical Kissing Number Problem as a cooperative matrix-completion game and trains a reinforcement learning system, PackingStar, in which two players fill and correct cosine entries to explore the broader extremal configuration space, opening a new path for this long-standing discrete geometry challenge.
